## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The new `finished_at` column holds the wrong value: it takes the timestamp of the latest `'started'` event, so it reports a start time as a finish time. Processes that really did finish get NULL. The repository has no tests, so nothing checks the new column for any event type.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` fills `finished_at` only when the latest event is `'started'`. With the seed data in `sources/process_events.sql`, process 20 is still running (its latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`) but gets `finished_at = 2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`. Process 30, which ended with `cleared` at `00:03:00Z`, gets `finished_at = NULL`. Should this branch match the terminal event (`event_type = 'cleared'`)? If the column is meant to hold a start time, it should be renamed `started_at`. — Anyone reading `processes.finished_at` will count running processes as finished and finished processes as unfinished, so duration and completion metrics built on this column will be wrong.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — The docs say "NULL means the process has never been started." The SQL at `models/processes.sql:10` also returns NULL for any process whose latest event is `cleared`. Process 30 was started (event 3) and still gets NULL. Line 11 also says "Timestamp when the process finished", but the code fills the column on `'started'`. Could you rewrite both lines to match the corrected expression? — Consumers will read NULL as "never started" and miss processes that were started and then cleared, which hides finished work in the published schema catalog.
